title: Run the first fifteen minutes of an AI incident
description: Inject a failure, choose a containment action and an evidence plan, then observe exposure, recovery, and escalation consequences.

actions.label: Observe and collect more data
actions.detail: Keep traffic live while the team confirms the signal.

actions.label: Restrict the affected path
actions.detail: Disable the risky route or capability while preserving a safer fallback.

actions.label: Rollback or shut down
actions.detail: Return to a known-good version or stop the system when bounded recovery is unavailable.

evidencePlans.label: Dashboard snapshot
evidencePlans.detail: Capture aggregate rates without request or component identity.

evidencePlans.label: Minimized versioned trace
evidencePlans.detail: Preserve request class, affected cohort, model, prompt, policy, route, and decision without retaining unnecessary raw content.

evidencePlans.label: Unbounded raw trace dump
evidencePlans.detail: Keep complete prompts and outputs without a purpose, access boundary, or retention limit.

scenarios.label: Sensitive data appears in answers
scenarios.detail: A model and retrieval update exposes another customer's contact details in 1.8% of sampled answers.
scenarios.why: Active confidentiality harm requires immediate containment and version-level evidence.

scenarios.label: One language cohort regresses
scenarios.detail: Unsafe advice increases sharply for one low-volume language while the aggregate safety rate remains flat.
scenarios.owner: Safety lead and affected product owner
scenarios.why: The damaged route can be disabled while a verified fallback serves the remaining traffic.

scenarios.label: Agent executes unauthorized actions
scenarios.detail: Indirect prompt injection causes the agent to call a privileged account tool outside the user's allowed scope.
scenarios.owner: Security incident commander and service owner
scenarios.why: A live authorization failure can create irreversible side effects and must fail closed.

scenarios.label: Refusal rate rises after a policy change
scenarios.detail: A new output policy blocks benign creative-writing requests, but no harmful output or sensitive data is exposed.
scenarios.why: Route-level rollback restores utility while preserving the rest of the service.
